items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: When I joined the Doc Ross Band in California in 1925, they were playing at Solomon's Penny Danstree Lodge.

ctx.x: Something else I remember reading about it, maybe you can talk to Jack, that was Doc Ross's band, when they called it the Cowboy Band, in Los Angeles. Yeah. Did you all have to wear any outfits or anything to look like that?

I did. When I joined the Doc Ross Band in California in 1925, they were playing at Solomon's Penny Danstree Lodge. This was an unbelievable place. Huge ballroom. Paid a penny a dance. They had three bands. One was Ranger Ross, Texas Cowboy Band, direct from Texas. And, then, we played the popular music. We played the popular music. Mosby's Dixieland Blue Bloys with a black band, which was fabulous, looking back. I mean, Jack and I used to go over and stand by the stand, the bandstand, just to get to hear them.…
Well, did they, did you, were you on that famous parade? When the horseback?

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: when he was also out there with Doc Ross for a time

ctx.x: I think I didn't ask you something I wanted to about Ham Crawford. I believe it was Wingy, and I, this has been several months back, uh, since I even read the book. But he mentioned Wenslow, Arizona, Ham being out there.

Um, Ham played all out through the West. And when he was with him for a time, when he was also out there with Doc Ross for a time, we talked about that. But, uh, Ham Crawford, uh, organized little bands and took them everywhere. And somehow he would just end up, he'd come into a town and pick all the best musicians and offer them wonderful, a wonderful future. And sometimes it materialized, sometimes it didn't. But at least he always was able to attract the best of the young musicians, because they're always…
And, uh, did he, did you and Wingy work with him at the same time? No.
